correctness.rationale: The inequalities define a full-dimensional normalized dual polytope; polarity exchanges its vertices with primal facets. Connectedness of the tight-edge graph is necessary by a small perturbation constant on a tight component missing the basepoint, and sufficient since tight differences are forced in both summands of a feasible midpoint and connectivity pins their potentials. A connected tight graph has a cross-cluster edge, so oscillation is precisely one and translation puts all potentials in [0,1]. A tight cross-edge must use endpoints 0 and 1, so every cluster contains one of them, but not both since t_i<1. In a lower cluster, every value is in [0,t_i] and a strict interior value would be isolated in the tight graph. The upper case is symmetric. Conversely opposite-class anchor sets form a connected complete bipartite subgraph, with each nonanchor joined tightly to the anchors of its own cluster. This also works for singleton blocks, all-anchor blocks, and coincidences between intermediate values of different clusters. The cluster signs and anchor sets are recovered after translating the minimum to zero. Thus the strict-region formula and the 98-facet example hold. At the simultaneous endpoint only the nonconstant normalized binary potentials are extreme, giving 2^N-2 (62 in that example). The frozen checker, inspected but not run, tests ten finite quarter-grid instances, whose tight spanning trees ensure quarter-integrality after normalization; it is not the proof for arbitrary scales.

evidence: For the split-zonotope sum, a generic exposing functional is given by leaf coefficients z_x with sum zero. Each signed split segment is maximized at the endpoint prescribed by the sign of the coefficient sum on one side. Thus, modulo constants, the exposed potential at x in A_i is ((1-t_i)/2) sign(sum_{y in A_i} z_y) + (t_i/2) sign(z_x). The two halves of each split can be represented by half its signed indicator difference, which modulo constants is the cluster or singleton indicator used in this expression.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Every vertex has a generic exposing functional, since one can perturb an interior normal off the finitely many split hyperplanes. The sign of a cluster sum must appear on at least one leaf in the cluster, and some cluster sums must be positive and some negative. Conversely, all choices satisfying those conditions are realizable: assign leaf coefficients of the required signs, make the leaves with the cluster sign dominate, and scale each cluster separately so the totals on positive and negative clusters cancel. Adding 1/2 to the exposed potentials gives exactly 0 or t_i in a lower cluster and 1-t_i or 1 in an upper cluster, with anchors the leaves of matching sign. The resulting choices are distinct and immediately count as (2^k-2) times the product of (2^{m_i}-1). Duplicate splits at k=2 or in singleton blocks impose no extra restriction beyond the same sign constraints. This is a direct endpoint calculation from the previously established exact zonotope representation, not just a resemblance to a broad method.

originality.rationale: The arbitrary cluster result is a direct specialization of the prior weighted compatible-split zonotope theorem for finite tree-like metrics (Delucchi–Hoessly, Theorem 3.1, explicitly restated by coauthor Hoessly in Theorem 3.6 of On some polytopes in phylogenetics).
